bilingual_equivalence.evidence: Both ask for focused separated slit images using ordinary thin lenses and provide the same one-focal-length/two-focal-length distances, zero/nonzero order choices and objective-plane detector alternative.

independent_solution_by_locale.zh: Using 1/f_c = 1/s + 1/s', slit distance s=f_c produces parallel rays, while s=2f_c gives a finite image s'=2f_c and nonparallel rays. A nonzero grating order has wavelength-dependent outgoing angles; zero order does not. A telescope objective receiving parallel bundles focuses them one objective focal length behind it, not at its own plane. Only b satisfies focused separated wavelength imaging: {b}.
independent_solution_by_locale.en: Independently applying the thin-lens relation, grating order relation and telescope focusing condition gives the same result. b uses the collimator focal-plane slit, a nonzero order and the objective back focal plane. a does not deliver the collimated bundles needed for that fixed detector focus, c lacks wavelength separation, and d lacks an image plane. Complete set {b}.

option_checks.evidence: At s=2f_c, the collimator gives s'=2f_c, not an image at infinity. Without unstated recollimation/refocusing, the telescope receives finite-vergence beams and their slit images are not focused at its fixed back focal plane. Recording a nonzero order does not fix that focus.

At s=f_c, the collimator sends parallel bundles to the grating. In a nonzero order different wavelengths leave at different angles and focus at separate positions in the telescope objective's back focal plane.

The focal placements can make a sharp zero-order image, but zero order has no wavelength-dependent grating separation. At normal incidence d sin(theta)=m lambda gives theta=0 for m=0. A focused but undispersed image fails the combined goal.

The objective plane intercepts bundles before their focused images form. The usual focused dispersed slit images are one objective focal length behind the lens; a detector at the lens plane does not receive them.

assumptions: Conventional paraxial slit-collimator-plane-grating-telescope optics with an accessible nonzero order.
Ordinary thin lenses and no extra correcting optics, focusing grating or angular resolving detector inserted into the alternatives.
A screen/image detector observes focused slit images, not a specially constructed pupil-plane Fourier measurement.
